source.author: lucan
source.text: Pax erat, et miles, castris permixtus utrisque, Errabat: duro concordes cespite mensas Institnunt, et permixto libamina Baccho Gramineis fluxere focis: iunctoque cubili Extrahit insomnes bellorum fabula noctes: Quo primum steterint campo, qua lancea dextra Exierit.
source.text_original: Pax erat, et miles, castris permixtus utrisque, / Errabat: duro concordes cespite mensas / Institnunt, et permixto libamina Baccho / Gramineis fluxere focis: iunctoque cubili / Extrahit insomnes bellorum fabula noctes: / Quo primum steterint campo, qua lancea dextra / Exierit.
source.text_english: There was peace, and the soldier, mingled with either camp, wandered about. They set up their tables on the hard turf in harmony, and offerings of mixed Bacchus flowed to grassy hearths; and in a shared bed the tale of the wars draws out sleepless nights: on what field they first stood, by what spear in the right hand it came forth.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Thracius hie noctem dulci testudine vates extrahit, ut steterit redimitus tempora vittis Phrixus et iniustas contectus nubibus aras fugerit Inoo linquens Athamanta Learcho; aureus ut iuvenem miserantibus intulit undis vector et astrictis ut sedit cornibus Helle.
reuse.text_original: Thracius hie noctem dulci testudine vates / extrahit, ut steterit redimitus tempora vittis / Phrixus et iniustas contectus nubibus aras / fugerit Inoo linquens Athamanta Learcho; / aureus ut iuvenem miserantibus intulit undis / vector et astrictis ut sedit cornibus Helle.
reuse.text_english: Here the Thracian singer passes the night with his sweet lyre, as Phrixus stood with his temples bound with fillets and, covered by the clouds, fled the unjust altars, leaving Athamas and Learcho for Ino; as the golden one bore the youth on the pitying waves, and as Helle sat upon the clasped horns.
